title: Dynamic Spectral Denoising with Global-Context Attention for Multi-Behavior Recommendation

problem.claim: Multi-behavior recommendation must exploit heterogeneous auxiliary feedback while handling behavior-dependent noise and inconsistency.

gap.claim: Existing representation processing is insufficient because intra-behavior entanglement resists coarse denoising and inter-behavior reliability varies across users and contexts, allowing unreliable signals to distort target intent.

contributions.claim: SpectraMB performs target-oriented representation purification before reliability-aware fusion.
Dynamic Feature-Level Spectral Filtering re-parameterizes embeddings into feature-frequency space and learns target-supervised, view-adaptive spectral modulation for component-wise purification.

Global-Context Attention Fusion uses a purified global representation to assess view compatibility and aggregate behaviors by reliability while retaining collaborative structure through a residual global backbone.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On three real-world datasets, the authors report that SpectraMB achieves the best results in most evaluation settings.
The authors report improved robustness under noisy interactions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-behavior recommendation uses heterogeneous auxiliary feedback, but noise and inconsistency undermine robustness.
The bottleneck is attributed to coupled intra-behavior representation entanglement and inter-behavior reliability heterogeneity.
SpectraMB purifies representations with dynamic feature-level spectral filtering before reliability-aware global-context fusion.
Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported to show strong results and improved robustness under noisy interactions.
